question.text: Which of the following is a key SEBI requirement for a Category III AIF that uses substantial leverage and short positions?

answer.text: Leverage must NOT exceed 2x of NAV; continuous monitoring with periodic disclosures of leverage and exposure, and next-working-day reporting/square-off of any breach.
Leverage is unlimited if disclosed in PPM.
Short selling is banned for Cat III AIFs.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI caps Cat III leverage at 2x of NAV (with exposure measured by the exposure/NAV formula), requires continuous leverage monitoring, periodic disclosures including custodian reporting, and next-working-day reporting and square-off if the 2x cap is breached. The Trap: Option B (unlimited if disclosed), Option C (short selling banned), and Option D (annual-only reporting) all misstate the regulatory regime. Note: The 2x cap, continuous monitoring, periodic disclosures, and breach handling work together as one regime rather than as separate annual obligations.
